gaps.sentence: He had hardly stepped off the plane ___ he was rushed into a meeting.
Far from resenting the changes, the staff welcomed them; ___, productivity rose.
gaps.explanation: Rising productivity is an additional point in the same direction: moreover.

gaps.sentence: ___ did he apologise, but he also refunded the full amount.
gaps.explanation: 'Not only did he..., but he also...' is the correlative pattern with inversion.

gaps.sentence: It sounds ___ the negotiations are close to a breakthrough.
gaps.explanation: 'It sounds as though...' reports an impression.

gaps.sentence: ___ it rains all weekend, the ceremony will still be held outdoors.
gaps.explanation: 'Even if' concedes a possible (not yet real) condition.

gaps.sentence: ___ being the youngest competitor, she won the gold medal.
gaps.explanation: 'Despite being...' is the standard concessive pattern with a gerund.

gaps.sentence: ___ a slight delay in Rome, the whole journey went smoothly.
gaps.explanation: 'Apart from' sets the delay aside as the only problem.

gaps.sentence: The treatment doesn't weaken patients; ___, it speeds up their recovery.
gaps.explanation: 'On the contrary' asserts the opposite of what was just said.
